identity.name: Zeitwerk
identity.one_liner: Lange's digital-jump hours-and-minutes display, driven by a patented constant-force escapement that releases stored energy once every sixty seconds to advance the discs cleanly.

narrative.story: The Zeitwerk, introduced in 2009, moved Lange into digital time display without giving up mechanical construction: hours and minutes jump on discs rather than sweep on hands, timed by a remontoir d'egalite that stores and releases energy in one-second increments so the discs advance instantly rather than dragging. Mechanically replicating a digital jump display of this size and legibility had defeated most manufactures before Lange committed a purpose-built movement to it.
narrative.collector_notes: The jump mechanism draws down power quickly; collectors check that the power-reserve indicator and the jump action stay synchronized, since a worn remontoir spring shows up first as a hesitant or double jump rather than a reserve-display error.
